requirement: The bundled requirements skill MUST direct agents adding or changing user-visible behavior in a Habeas project to draft stable requirement IDs and exact text, obtain the user's agreement, and install the agreed requirements in the mdBook before writing implementation or test code. It MUST direct agents to review substantive changes to agreed obligations with the user. The bootstrap skill MUST require user review of requirements inferred from existing code before installing them. The evidence skill MUST allow truthful false determinations while implementation is pending.
rationale: The Symposium manifest distributes the requirements, bootstrap, and evidence skills. Their instructions require review of exact requirement text before implementation and permit truthful pending evidence.

name: habeas-requirements
description: Design and vet requirements and examples for user-visible behavior changes in a Habeas mdBook project before coding; maintain definitions and references.
# Habeas requirements
## New or changed behavior

When a user requests new or changed user-visible behavior in a Habeas project, first read the relevant requirements, code, and tests. Identify requirements that already express the intended behavior. For gaps, draft the smallest set of observable obligations, including important outcomes and failure cases, without committing to an implementation.

Run `habeas info <full-requirement-name>` to read a requirement's current text, evidence state, rationale, inputs, and validation findings as Markdown. The selector also accepts a regular expression over full requirement names when you need to inspect a group.

Show the user the full IDs and text of existing requirements to reuse, plus the proposed chapter location, full IDs, and exact fenced text of any additions or changes. State open product choices separately. Ask the user to agree to or revise this requirement set. User-provided exact requirement text or explicit agreement earlier in the conversation counts as approval; a general request to build the feature does not. Keep drafts out of the mdBook while review is pending, and do not write implementation or test code yet.

After agreement, install the approved requirements in the mdBook and confirm their names. Then implement the behavior, add tests and traceability references, and maintain evidence. If implementation reveals a substantive change to an approved obligation, review and install the revised requirement before coding that change. Use the evidence skill for pending determinations while implementation is incomplete.
Exclude generated and third-party code from the inventories. If a candidate looks user-facing but its purpose is unclear, keep it on the gap list until resolved.

Treat requirements inferred from existing code as proposals. Show the user their proposed full IDs and exact text, along with uncertainty about whether observed behavior is intended or a bug. Obtain agreement on the proposals before installing them in the mdBook; prior explicit agreement to the same requirements counts.

Create or reuse the agreed, stable, chapter-qualified `{req}` requirements in the mdBook. State observable obligations with BCP 14 terms. Group tests that check the same behavior under one requirement; several tests MAY share an ID. For tests of internal invariants, write a requirement for the invariant they actually check rather than inventing a user-facing promise. Distinguish intended behavior from a possible bug or incidental implementation detail.

For each requirement or example, maintain `evidence/<full-name>.json` with exactly `determination`, `rationale`, `inputs`, and a text field matching the directive: `requirement` for `{req}` or `example` for `{example}`. Copy the current Markdown between the directive's opening and closing fences into that text field, excluding leading and trailing whitespace. Set `determination` to `true` only after checking the behavior; otherwise use `false` and explain the remaining work in `rationale`.

An approved requirement or example may be installed before its implementation exists. Record it with `determination: false` and a rationale describing the pending work; an empty `inputs` array is valid until there are lines to cite. Expect validation to fail during this interval. Once code and tests satisfy the approved definition, inspect them, snapshot their exact lines, and only then change the determination to `true`. Review a substantive change to an approved obligation with the user before changing its requirement text.

Each input names a repository-relative `file`, a 1-based inclusive `line_start` and `line_end`, and a `text` array containing the exact current text of those lines. Cite the lines that support the determination. Every `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to the definition must fall within one of its input ranges.
